Grassy. That is not the word I have. I have meadow, meadowland, the meadow where the lava flows. I hunt there, and I fly there, and I rest there. I have no word for grassy. Grassy place. That is not a word I know. The meadow is what I call it, and I hunt it at dusk, when the mice come out. I sit on the fence and wait, and when they run, I fly down and catch them. I have never seen a mouse that runs the other way.

Grassy. That is the place where the wind moves. I know the wind, but not the grass. I have a hollow in the oak, and a meadow beyond it. I do not know what lies between. I hear the wind and the mice. I hear the meadow and the lava. I do not know the grass.
